name: Plank
pattern: Anti-extension hold: face down on forearms (or hands) and toes, the body stays one straight line while the trunk resists sagging.
setup: Forearms on the floor, elbows under your shoulders.
Legs straight, on your toes, feet hip width.
Squeeze your glutes, brace your belly, head in line with your back.

steps.text: Hold one straight line from head to heels and breathe steadily. Stop when the line breaks.

cues.cue: One straight line, head to heels.
cues.why: The prone bridge is an anti-extension hold; a neutral line lets the abdominals carry the load.

cues.cue: Tuck the tailbone slightly and squeeze your glutes.
cues.why: A posterior pelvic tilt with glutes on, elbows reaching forward (long lever), raised abdominal activity well above a standard plank.

cues.cue: Elbows under the shoulders; push the floor away.
cues.why: Pushing through the forearms keeps the shoulder blades set and spreads load to the serratus.
A moderate brace is enough to stiffen the trunk; you should still be able to breathe.

cues.cue: Quality over time: short sets with a perfect line.
cues.why: Endurance holds are timed only while form holds; once the line breaks, the test (and the set) is over.

breathing: Breathe slowly and evenly; do not hold your breath.

tempo.note: Hold 10-30 s, rest, repeat. Add time only while the line stays straight.

mistakes.name: Hips sag
mistakes.looks: The low back arches and the hips drop toward the floor.
mistakes.fix: Squeeze glutes, tuck the tailbone, brace.
mistakes.why: The spine hangs into extension instead of being held.

mistakes.name: Hips too high
mistakes.looks: The body makes a tent with the hips highest.
mistakes.fix: Lower the hips until shoulders, hips and heels line up.

mistakes.name: Head drops
mistakes.looks: The head hangs and the chin points down.
mistakes.fix: Look at the floor just ahead of your hands.
mistakes.why: It breaks the line and rounds the upper back.

safety: Shoulder pain: plank on the hands from a bench (incline) or on the knees.
High blood pressure: keep breathing; use short holds.

variants.change: Hands on a bench or wall: easier.
Lifting a limb removes a support: the trunk must also resist rotation; keep hips level.

variants.when: walk|up and down|walk up|to push up|dynamic
variants.change: Moving between forearms and hands: keep hips still while the arms move.
Plate on the back: harder; keep the same line.

subtypes.name: High plank and shoulder taps
subtypes.match: on hands|push.?up position|shoulder tap|tap|walk|up and down|to push|knee tap|hit the ball|pass through|pull
subtypes.change: On straight arms, hands under shoulders; for taps lift one hand to the opposite shoulder without the hips rocking.

subtypes.name: Hollow hold and rock
subtypes.change: On your back, low back pressed down, shoulders and straight legs just off the floor, arms by the ears.

subtypes.name: Reverse plank
subtypes.change: Face up on hands or forearms and heels, hips lifted level with shoulders and ankles.

subtypes.name: Bear plank
subtypes.change: On hands and toes with knees bent 90 degrees and hovering a few centimetres off the floor.

motion.basis: Body line and elbow under shoulder from the standard prone bridge (ekstrom2007); trunk 84 because shoulders sit a forearm's height above the toes (estimate). Dynamic and hollow subtype angles are estimates.
